title: NAB Show: TAG Video Systems, Oracle Partner on Cloud Monitoring
body_html:
What Was Announced

The recent NAB Show saw the announcement of a partnership between TAG Video Systems and Oracle, focused on cloud monitoring. This collaboration aims to integrate TAG's expertise in real-time media performance monitoring with Oracle's cloud infrastructure, providing a comprehensive solution for media companies to oversee their cloud-based operations. By combining forces, the two companies seek to address the growing need for efficient and reliable monitoring of media workflows in the cloud, which is becoming increasingly crucial as more broadcasters and media organizations migrate their operations to cloud-based environments.

The Engineering and Operational Significance

This partnership is significant because it tackles a critical challenge in cloud-based media workflows: the ability to monitor and manage performance in real-time, across multiple platforms and geographic locations. By leveraging Oracle's cloud infrastructure, TAG's monitoring solutions can provide media companies with a unified view of their operations, enabling them to quickly identify and resolve issues, and optimize their workflows for better efficiency and reliability. The integration of TAG's monitoring capabilities with Oracle's cloud infrastructure also enables the use of advanced analytics and machine learning techniques to predict and prevent potential issues, reducing downtime and improving overall system resilience. Furthermore, this partnership has the potential to simplify the deployment and management of cloud-based media workflows, allowing engineering teams to focus on higher-level tasks and improving overall operational efficiency.

Industry Context

The partnership between TAG and Oracle is part of a broader trend in the media industry, where companies are increasingly looking to cloud-based solutions to improve the flexibility, scalability, and cost-effectiveness of their operations. As more media organizations migrate their workflows to the cloud, the need for robust monitoring and management tools has become more pressing. Other companies, such as Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure, are also investing heavily in cloud-based media solutions, highlighting the growing importance of this sector. The TAG-Oracle partnership is notable, however, because it brings together two companies with deep expertise in media monitoring and cloud infrastructure, respectively, and has the potential to set a new standard for cloud-based media workflow management. Additionally, this partnership reflects the ongoing shift towards IP-based workflows, as outlined in standards such as SMPTE ST 2110, and the growing adoption of cloud-based playout and ingest solutions, which require robust monitoring and management capabilities to ensure reliable and high-quality output.

Implications for Broadcast and Media Teams

For broadcast and media teams, the TAG-Oracle partnership has significant implications, particularly in terms of the potential to simplify and optimize cloud-based workflows. Engineering teams, in particular, should take note of this development, as it may enable them to streamline their monitoring and management processes, and improve overall system reliability. Operations managers should also consider the potential benefits of this partnership, including the ability to reduce downtime, improve predictive maintenance, and enhance overall operational efficiency. Furthermore, platform teams responsible for overseeing the deployment and management of cloud-based media workflows should evaluate the TAG-Oracle solution in the context of their existing workflows, and consider the potential benefits of integrating this solution into their operations. By doing so, they can determine whether this partnership can help address specific pain points or workflow bottlenecks, and improve overall performance and reliability. Ultimately, the success of this partnership will depend on its ability to deliver tangible benefits to media companies, in terms of cost savings, improved efficiency, and enhanced reliability, and its potential to set a new standard for cloud-based media workflow management.
